newBatches.title: Machine storage and the quarantine record
newBatches.cliChanges: A `storage` block on `status`: byte totals for ~/.terum/skills/{teams,cache,quarantine,evals} by recursive stat, plus a quarantine inventory of {when,name,reason,bytes}. CP-S1: moveToQuarantine (src/lib/placer.ts:170) is the SINGLE funnel and its directory name is new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g,'-') (placer.ts:171), so one sidecar quarantine/<timestamp>/reason.json beside the moved folder records why (drift, a connect --keep-repo resolution, a team leave clone) and by which verb. That sidecar is a new state file in the store tree, not a field in people/<handle>.json or config.json: the one SIMPLE condition both rows break. Two sections move together, §6's status bullet and §4.2's local-state tree block, which does not name evals/ (machine uninstall sweeps run/cache/teams/quarantine, not evals/). Machine-local, never committed, no guard action, no safeWrite. The one drawn reason that cannot occur stays a design edit.
newBatches.appHalf: Settings ▸ Machine's storage rows and the quarantine card render real bytes and a real reason instead of the fixture's '42 KB'/'1.1 MB', and the drawn path shape quarantine/<timestamp>/<name> becomes literally what is on disk. RM-05's quarantine read (S7g appHalf) consumes this inventory instead of reversing the [:.]→- substitution itself — removing the plan's only place where the app re-derives a CLI filename rule.
newBatches.approver: Ryan (phase-1 §6 status + §4.2 local-state tree — two sections, which is the MEDIUM)
newBatches.rationale: Same MEDIUM shape, same board, same verb. The app-side route is impossible, not merely forbidden: the documented Tauri fs plugin surface has no size or metadata call, so the drawn byte figures cannot be produced app-side at all. Escape hatch to offer in the PR body: drop evals/ and §4.2 need not move, restoring condition (5) at the cost of two drawn rows.
newBatches.risk: The sidecar must never be treated as authoritative when absent — every pre-existing quarantine folder has none, so the UI shows path and date with no reason rather than inventing one. The scan must not follow symlinks and one unreadable subtree must cost its own row, not the verb.
newBatches.tests: status.test.ts: totals for a seeded store; 0 with no error for an absent subtree; one unreadable subtree costs that row only. placer.test.ts: moveToQuarantine writes reason.json beside the moved folder and the folder is byte-identical to the source. sync.test.ts: --prune deletes the sidecar with its folder.
newBatches.syncRule: Read-only except the sidecar, written at the moment the folder moves and never after. Nothing is committed, so nothing propagates: another machine's quarantine stays invisible, exactly as MC-04's ruling requires.

newBatches.title: The one Ajay §12 paragraph: what a display surface may do
newBatches.cliChanges: ZERO CODE in all five. One §12 paragraph, written as an ENUMERATION of what is permitted rather than a relaxation of 'The receipt JSON is the API. The UI never runs evals and never derives new statistics' — a broad relaxation licenses the app to invent statistics generally, which is the thing that sentence exists to prevent. Permit exactly: (a) EV-01/EV-16 — a surface may render a receipt's own comparisons[*].net_lift at card altitude and may list more than one receipt per version, provided each receipt's provenance sits beside its own numbers and no two are merged into one figure; (b) EV-02 — a viewer may TRIGGER a run through a terminal hand-off, never an in-app agent spawn (D27's second branch); (c) EV-09 — a per-machine forecast from ONE receipt's own per-arm means, suppressed when the configured arm model differs from receipt.provenance.model (receipt.ts:74-85); (d) EV-19 — a coverage/verdict tally over the latest receipt at each skill's current tree with a provenance stamp. EV-16 additionally needs §5.4 and §12 amended TOGETHER, since both carry the identical latest-receipt-per-version sentence.
newBatches.appHalf: EV-19's app half flips FORBIDDEN → SIMPLE the moment the paragraph lands, and is one walk of the clone: skills/*/SKILL.md for the denominator, git rev-parse HEAD:skills/<name> per key, then the newest schema-valid receipt under evals/<id>/<tree>/. EV-01 moves the lift figure onto the card. EV-09 renders the forecast labelled as pricing arm runs only, and renders nothing on the no-receipt state. EV-16's rail lists a version's committed runs and opens one at a time, never two side by side in one number.
newBatches.approver: Ajay — one message, one paragraph, five rows
newBatches.rationale: The highest-leverage sentence in M7: one paragraph unblocks five rows, four of them MEDIUM, and turns the app's whole evals surface from fixture-backed to receipt-backed. It costs no code, which is why it should be asked for first even though it is reviewed late. Teddy's call moves EV-01 here from the design walk, so the lift figure stays on the card as drawn.
newBatches.risk: Written as a relaxation instead of an enumeration it becomes a licence to compute; written without the §5.4 twin it makes §12 contradict §5.4. Both failure modes live in the wording, not the build.
newBatches.tests: No CLI tests. App-side: a fixture invariant asserting every rendered figure is a receipt field printed at the receipt's own precision (toFixed(3) for sign_p), and a test proving a receipt from a different (provenance.model, cc_version) pair is EXCLUDED rather than compared.

newBatches.title: App-only seam mechanics: change notification and driving setup
newBatches.cliChanges: NONE, and for RM-24 that is a RULE rather than an omission: §6.1 makes setup a sequencer that cannot skip, pre-answer or batch a delegated verb's consent, with a §12 test proving it, so an option to suppress a prompt must not be asked for. setup already records only reached steps (src/commands/setup.ts:47-48, steps: Partial<Record<Step, StepOutcome>>) and returns them inside the FAILURE value (:71-72), so an interrupted run already hands its caller its stopping point. RM-23's CLI half is likewise closed: stampPath is exported and ConfigStore.read returns the parsed config with its pending array.
newBatches.appHalf: RM-23 is a new adapter mechanism: Backend.subscribe plus invalidation keyed by source (config, clone:<team>, placed, stamp:<team>), revalidate-on-visible, a low-frequency poll of the two cheap local reads, an explicit Sync now, a ≥250 ms debounce ignoring .lock directories and config.json.<pid>.<uuid>.tmp files, and NO optimistic cache writes. Two forcing facts: config.ts writes by atomic rename so the watched file is REPLACED and a path watch alone misses every change; and a clean no-op sync's only trace is the stamp write. RM-24 is four pieces: the Prompter rendering the drawn wizard dialog, a hand-written 9→6 mapping from SetupResult.steps onto the drawn step map, print-only steps as screen copy, and a hard-coded false to the gh offer.
newBatches.rationale: Both are app-only MEDIUMs whose CLI halves are CLOSED, so they belong to the adapter and must never become asks. They are a batch rather than a prose disposition because RM-23's subscribe mechanism is what every other app row's freshness depends on and has no other owner.
newBatches.risk: RM-23 is the one place a timer can creep in. An app-initiated sync writes run/<team>.stamp and suppresses the real SessionStart hook for an hour (stampIsFresh, src/commands/sync.ts:135), so a polling refresh that syncs is a product bug, not a performance choice.
newBatches.tests: A subscribe test proving a config rename fires exactly one invalidation; a no-op sync fires the stamp invalidation and nothing else; a setup-drive test proving every printed step maps to a drawn step and that the gh offer is answered false.
newBatches.syncRule: Poll the two cheap local reads only; never sync on a timer. The standing rule in the sync addendum binds this batch above all others.

newBatches.title: The `new` verb: a destination for the drawn New skill action
newBatches.cliChanges: ONE new verb, `new <name>`, scaffolding a local skill folder under the placement root. The name is validated by isSkillName (src/lib/schema.ts:19, /^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/ and length ≤ 64) — the same rule connect enforces — and an existing folder is refused. It writes a SKILL.md carrying name and a non-empty description and NOTHING ELSE: it must not write license, metadata.id, metadata.author or metadata.terum-category, because those four are connect's managed fields and a hand-written id is the one value that can collide with a real skill. It takes the placement-root lock (the correction to the coster's draft: ~/.claude/skills is where install and sync write, so an existing-folder race is real), touches no team repository, needs no guard action and no safeWrite, and prints `connect <path>` as its last line.
newBatches.appHalf: The Library's New skill CTA and the two empty-state pairs keep their drawn label and gain a real destination. The board debt is real and must be paid before it ships: no board draws name / description / scope / what-happens-next, and the second step must say honestly that a new folder is LOCAL, fails validate until connected (src/cli.ts:114), and blocks install <name> for a same-named team skill. The zero-new-board alternative is relabelling the CTA to Connect — connect with no path is already a picker (src/cli.ts:122).
newBatches.rationale: Teddy's decision (a): the New skill CTA stays on the canvas, so the verb has to exist. SIMPLE on every condition — no owner-file field, one verb, no guard change, tests in the existing layout, one paragraph, one approver. Placed after S7p because S7p is the last batch to touch the frontmatter parse this verb writes against.
newBatches.risk: The verb must not write the four managed fields, or a hand-authored skill reaches connect already carrying an id connect is supposed to mint. The name-collision consequence (costing row RM-37, costing:1321) is a product fact the board must state; the verb cannot prevent it.
newBatches.tests: new.test.ts: creates a folder whose SKILL.md fails validate only on the managed fields; refuses an invalid name, an existing folder and a name colliding with a placed skill; writes no team-repo path and takes no safeWrite; prints connect <path> in the caller's invocation form.
newBatches.syncRule: A new folder is untracked until connect runs: ls --local reports tracked: false (S7g) and sync never touches it, because sync's placement loop iterates config.placements (src/commands/sync.ts:200) and a scaffolded folder has no entry.

newBatches.cliChanges: --cwd <path> on install (src/cli.ts:125), uninstall-skill (:126) and sync (:128). COST CORRECTION verified this session: the args already exist and are already threaded — InstallArgs.cwd, UninstallArgs.cwd, SyncArgs.cwd — and args.cwd is already consumed inside sync's placement loop, where matchingProjectRoot(clone, entry.scope.project, runner, args.cwd) is called at src/commands/sync.ts:206 and the project placement is skipped at :209 when no matching root is found. Only the three commander registrations and the pass-through are missing. NO project→checkout-path map is added: a recorded path is a second answer to a question the worktree already answers, and it goes stale the moment a checkout moves.
newBatches.appHalf: One --cwd <root> call per project root the app knows about, merged with the global-root call under the CLI's own precedence rule, plus the caption stating the nearest-repository narrowing. The root set is derivable from config.placements keys, which are absolute placed paths carrying scope {kind:'project', project}.
newBatches.approver: Ryan — and it must be presented AS a MEDIUM, not inside a SIMPLE bundle
newBatches.rationale: Isolated out of S7c on the judges' finding: this is the one row whose CLI half knowingly breaks the bar's flag-count condition (three flags on three verbs), and it must not ride inside a batch presented as SIMPLE. Alone, the bar-break is the only thing litigated and the cost correction above is the strongest available framing.

newBatches.tests: install/sync/uninstall tests: --cwd resolves the project from the named checkout, not the process cwd; an absent path fails with the path named; --cwd outside any git repository behaves exactly as the same run from that directory would.
newBatches.syncRule: --cwd changes only which worktree matchingProjectRoot resolves (called at sync.ts:206). The project-placement rule at sync.ts:209 is unchanged, so a project placement outside its checkout stays SKIPPED rather than quarantined.

newBatches.title: Decision: how npx hands off to the desktop app
newBatches.cliChanges: NOTHING IS BUILT — three options costed, plus the evidence that no mechanism exists today: src/lib/launch.ts only DESCRIBES the executing entry (describeLaunch at launch.ts:14 over the Launch union at :5-10, kinds npx|local|global|source|unknown); there is no spawn, no download and no install-location convention anywhere in the CLI. OPTION A, release-asset download: a new `app` verb (or a setup step) resolves the platform asset from the GitHub release, verifies a checksum, unpacks to a stated location and prints it — costs a network fetch on a verb that has none, a checksum policy, an unpack path outside §4.2's enumerated tree (so machine uninstall must sweep it), and macOS quarantine on an unsigned artifact. OPTION B, bundled binary in the npm tarball: refused on inspection — per-platform binaries in one tarball, and both the files list and the duplicated CI/release must-have arrays would have to carry them. OPTION C, URL hand-off: setup's epilogue and an `app` verb print or open the releases page. Zero mechanism, honest today, and the only option that ships without spending a phase gate.
newBatches.appHalf: Whichever option wins is what the drawn onboarding means by 'open the app'. Until then the app must not claim the CLI can launch it, and CP-O2's onboarding string stays a design-side call.
newBatches.approver: Teddy decides the route; Ryan approves whichever one becomes a verb
newBatches.rationale: Teddy's decision (d). This is a real fork with a phase gate behind it: TJ-08 ('setup opens the app') is deferred twice in the phase-1 spec, and the costing's reason is exactly this — the launcher needs an install-location convention, which is a phase-2 mechanism decision. It is in the plan so the decision has an owner and a place, not so anything gets built.
newBatches.risk: Option A quietly makes the CLI a package manager for a second artifact, with a sweep obligation and a signing story attached. Option C is the only one that cannot rot, and it is also the only one that ships before M5 gives the app a stable install location.
newBatches.tests: None until a route is chosen. Option C's whole test is one string assertion in setup.test.ts.

syncDesignAddendum:
ADDENDUM. The thesis holds — a new people-file field propagates with ZERO sync code, because personSchema is passthrough and sync re-serializes the whole parsed object while appending only to installed/declined. Four additions, one set of corrections.

R1 — BINDING ON EVERY FUTURE PEOPLE-FILE WRITER, not a note on one batch. No writer of people/<you>.json may construct an object literal or capture the document outside the mutation: read the PRE-IMAGE inside the mutation, parse with personSchema, mutate ONE field, re-serialize. safeWrite re-applies against a freshly fetched pre-image and re-runs guard inside the loop, so a capturing writer turns field-level last-writer-wins into WHOLE-DOCUMENT last-writer-wins and a concurrent role edit is silently clobbered by a projects edit. Binds profile and decline (S7b), favorite and follow (S7t), and everything after.

R1's TEST is the acceptance criterion for the thesis: a people file carrying role and projects survives a full cycle (install, orphan adopt, orphan decline) with both fields byte-identical, plus a two-writer test where one --role and one --project both land. Testing the writer alone does not catch the next writer.

PF-05 — 'Last active' is a DERIVATION, not a field (Teddy, c). git log -1 --format=%cI -- people/<handle>.json, one pass for the roster on the full unshallow clone, the same shape as PF-06's joined.
